newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: African officials prepare for Zimbabwe OAU summit.
newsitem.headline: African officials prepare for Zimbabwe OAU summit.

text.p: African officials met on Monday to prepare for an Organisation of African Unity summit in Harare next week expected to be attended by more than 40 leaders, including Laurent Kabila of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Until Kabila's forces drove long-serving president Mobutu Sese Seko out earlier this month, OAU officials were expecting the conference in Zimbabwe's capital to be dominated by the fight for power in former Zaire, Africa's third largest country.

"We will still discuss the Zaire situation...but now the focus will be on the transition to democracy and how to resolve other conflicts on the continent," OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim told reporters.

The situation in Sierra Leone, where the army staged a coup against the democratically elected government of Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on Sunday, would also feature prominently in pre-summit talks this week.

"We would like to hear the views of the governments in that (Western African) region, but I would certainly hope that we take a very strong stance against this development," he said of the coup, saying he hoped the new leaders would not be welcomed into the OAU ranks.

"It is lamentable that some soldiers who have no mandate to rule at all should decide to challenge the legitimate position of the people. It is a setback for Africa's transition to democracy," Salim said.

OAU officials and organisers from Zimbabwe's host government told reporters this week's two-day meeting of African ambassadors to the OAU would discuss the agenda of an OAU foreign ministerial council opening later this week, and look at housekeeping issues ahead of the June 2-4 summit.
The summit is returning to southern Africa a quarter of a century after Zambia hosted one in 1972.

Zimbabwe Foreign Affairs Minister Stan Mudenge said the meetings would also focus on current peace efforts in Angola and Somalia, the war in Sudan and establishment of an African Court of Human Rights.
The other big issue would be the election of an OAU secretary-general, Mudenge said.
Salim, a former Tanzanian prime minister who has headed the 53-member OAU since 1989, is seeking a third four-year term and is being challenged by Ivorian Foreign Minister Amara Essy.
